Package frc.lib.NinjasLib.swerve

Class Swerve

java.lang.Object
frc.lib.NinjasLib.swerve.Swerve
public class Swerve extends Object
Manages a 4-module swerve drivetrain: hardware/simulation setup, acceleration- and speed-limited driving via drive(frc.lib.NinjasLib.swerve.SwerveSpeeds), odometry feeding, and module/gyro access. Accessed as a singleton through get()/setInstance(frc.lib.NinjasLib.swerve.Swerve); most callers should go through SwerveController rather than this class directly.

    • drive

      public void drive(SwerveSpeeds input)
      The primary entry point for commanding the drivetrain: this is the method every driver control loop and autonomous routine should call each periodic cycle to move the robot. Drives the swerve towards the given speeds, subject to acceleration and speed limiting, and commands the resulting module states.

      The requested input is not applied directly; it is treated as a target that wantedSpeeds accelerates towards, bounded by the configured forward, skid and rotational acceleration/speed limits. If auto-lock is enabled in SwerveConstants.Special.enableAutoLock and the input stays within the jitter prevention deadband for SwerveConstants.Special.autoLockFrames consecutive calls, this method locks the wheels in an X pattern via lockWheelsToX() and resets wantedSpeeds instead of driving. On a real robot the final chassis speeds are discretized (see ChassisSpeeds.discretize(double, double, double, double)) to compensate for the 20 ms command loop before being converted to module states. This method is a no-op if the swerve was constructed disabled (see get()).

      Parameters:
      input - the desired velocity, angular velocity, and whether it is field- or robot-relative

    • periodic

      public void periodic()
      Must be called once per robot loop cycle (e.g. from Robot.robotPeriodic() or a subsystem's periodic()). Applies any pending initial pose, refreshes gyro/module inputs and feeds odometry (directly, or by draining the odometry thread's buffered samples if SwerveConstants.Special.enableOdometryThread is set), and logs current/wanted velocities. A no-op if this swerve was constructed disabled.
